headline: Law renews federal firefighter grant programs and the U.S. Fire Administration, and changes how the government licenses and supports nuclear energy.
what_it_does: The law funds the U.S. Fire Administration through 2028 and extends three major grant programs for fire departments through 2030. It also directs the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to speed up and update how it licenses nuclear reactors, especially newer advanced reactors, micro-reactors, and reactors on old coal or polluted sites. It lowers some licensing fees for advanced reactor applicants until 2030 and limits nuclear fuel made by Russian- or Chinese-controlled companies. It also gives the NRC new hiring and pay powers and requires many reports to Congress.

who_it_affects.how: Federal grants for equipment, fire prevention, and staffing are extended through 2030, and a government audit will look at barriers departments face in getting federal money.
They pay lower NRC licensing fees until September 30, 2030, may qualify for Energy Department prizes equal to their fees, and can use faster licensing processes.
They need an NRC license to own or possess fuel made abroad by Russian- or Chinese-controlled companies, and the license is barred if the Energy and State Departments find a national security threat.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign companies from allied countries and India
who_it_affects.how: Companies tied to OECD member countries or India may get licenses to own or run U.S. nuclear facilities if the NRC finds no threat to security or public safety.

who_it_affects.group: Communities with retired coal plants or polluted brownfield sites
who_it_affects.how: The NRC must look at ways to make it easier to license nuclear facilities at these locations.
Fusion machines will be regulated under rules for radioactive byproduct material rather than the framework for fission reactors.
Until 2034, the NRC can hire up to 210 highly skilled staff outside normal civil service rules and pay hiring and performance bonuses.
The NRC must create a training subprogram within its University Nuclear Leadership Program for nuclear workforce needs.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 9, 2024; fire programs extended through FY2028–FY2030, reduced reactor fees end September 30, 2030, and special NRC hiring authority ends September 30, 2034.
